facts.raw_span: A 34-year-old Thai man
history of hypertension and tobacco use disorder
family history significant for polycythemia, hypertension, and stroke in his father
worsening bifrontal headaches, nausea, vomiting, and right-sided blurry vision
blood pressures in the emergency department ranged from 180 to 190/80-90 mm Hg
National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score was 2 because of complete left homonymous hemianopsia
hemoglobin 20.2 g/dL, hematocrit 54.8%, MCV 74 fL, and thrombocytopenia (91,000/mm³)
CT Head: Left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage with intravascular extension
CT Head: Right posterior parietal intraparenchymal hemorrhage (4.7 × 2.9 × 4.2 cm) with blood product in the right lateral ventricle and minimal midline shift
Hb E: 34.0%  Hb Tak: 59.9%
not adherent to his antihypertensive regimen
missing a few doses of his carvedilol and had cut down on his smoking
